harbor-two-pages.pdf.content:
The Harbor Archive

The old lighthouse stood above the harbor, where visitors often gathered to watch the boats come in.

At sunset the fog rolled past the well-known lighthouse, hiding the boats from view.

The harbor master wrote down the weather at six.

The waves rose against the wall as the wind picked up.

The archive was open to everyone who lived in the town.

Some visitors arrived long before the tour began.

Everyone waited outside until the keeper turned the key.

The keeper explained that the light had guided ships through the narrow channel for over a century. She kept a record of each rescue in a leather journal.

The First Rescue

The crew followed a signal from the harbor and recovered the missing sailboat before dawn.

The captain thanked everyone for their help.

A Morning at the Community Garden

We planted the tomatoes near the path and watered them before lunch. A robin waited on the fence.

The gardener opened the west gate and brought a basket of seeds. We promised to share the harvest.
